prompt.brief: Design a predictive autoscaling system that forecasts service demand, combines predictions with safety limits and current capacity, and proactively scales infrastructure without causing oscillation or runaway cost.
successSignals: Separate observed metrics, forecasts, scaling policy, capacity reservations, actuator commands, and resulting health signals.
Forecast multiple horizons with confidence bands, combine prediction with reactive safeguards, and smooth actions with cooldowns.
Coordinate dependent services in an order that preserves capacity and avoid scaling on corrupted, delayed, or feedback-loop data.
Explain cold start, event-driven spikes, model drift, quota failure, rollback, cost budgets, and manual override.

functional: Collect service metrics and calendars, produce forecasts, evaluate confidence, and calculate a bounded desired capacity.
Apply scale-up and scale-down actions across dependent services with approvals, cooldowns, health checks, and audit history.
Expose forecast, recommendation, actual capacity, action result, cost, model version, and manual override state.
nonFunctional: Target demand forecast error within 15% on declared workloads while reactive utilization limits protect the SLO.
Scale decisions for thousands of services with dependency-aware queues and per-service rate and cost limits.
Make forecast publication and actuator commands idempotent and require observed state before repeating a scale action.
Fall back to reactive autoscaling and safe capacity floors when forecasts, metrics, or provider APIs fail.
scaleAssumptions: Manage 10,000 services across regions with minute-level signals and burst events such as launches or campaigns.
Partition forecasts by service, region, and horizon; isolate noisy services and coordinated dependency groups.
Retain metrics, feature cutoffs, forecasts, actions, policy versions, outcomes, and cost evidence for replay.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Predictive autoscaling system commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Predictive autoscaling system writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Predictive autoscaling system version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Predictive autoscaling system by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Predictive autoscaling system work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Predictive autoscaling system projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Predictive autoscaling system projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Predictive autoscaling system records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Predictive autoscaling system latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
